body_markdown:
Porsche is working on a successor to the 918 Spyder hybrid hypercar, and it will be powered by an engine not seen since the Sixties. That’s according to Germany’s[Handelsblatt](https://www.handelsblatt.com/unternehmen/industrie/volkswagen-nach-gewinnwarnung-weitere-4000-jobs-bei-porsche-entbehrlich/100254633.html) , which reports that the new model will be powered by a flat-eight engine. The suspected price tag: half a million Euros, or $575,000.


*Handelsblatt* also states that the project is known inside Porsche as codename “S1” and could be revealed to investors as early as its Capital Markets Day on October 7.


In Porsche’s past, for Formula 1, the automaker developed a flat-eight-powered engine designed by Hans Metzger and Hans Honich. The 1.5-liter “Type 753” motor developed 185 hp and was responsible for Porsche’s only F1 race win as a constructor. Dan Gurney was behind the wheel of the 804 single-seater when he took the checkered flag at the French Grand Prix in 1962.


A 2.0-liter version, known as the Type 771, also powered Porsche’s endurance racing efforts in the 718 W-RS, 904/8, 906, 907, 909, and 910 from 1962 to 1968. From 1968, a new three-liter flat-eight motor, the 908, came into play—a further development of the 916 flat-six.


Porsche 771 flat-eight engine, displacing 2.0-liters and built for endurance racing.


Morio/Creative Commons


All these engines were built for the track only, but Porsche did experiment with squeezing an eight into a road car, building two[914/8s](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/porsche-914-s-prototype-specs-history-pictures/) . One was a concept, while the second was a 60th birthday gift to Ferry Porsche.


The upcoming S1 would be the first production Porsche with eight cylinders, but as yet there is only speculation concerning its specifications.[Porsche eFuels](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/can-e-fuels-save-classic-cars/) Project Manager Marcos Marquez previously confessed to *The Intercooler* that the company had once built a 5.0-liter, twin-turbo, 750-hp flat-eight and fitted it to a Cayman chassis. Could this be the engine that’s being resurrected?


When it comes to the S1’s design and styling, the 2016 Porsche Le Mans Living Legend concept car (below) may offer some clues, or the 919 Street show car (top), built in 2017. However it looks, one thing’s for sure: it should sound amazing.
